patch_description: The current program's weakest metrics are slope_changes (162.8), false_reversals (125), and smoothness (0.11), while lag_error (0.29) and correlation (0.94) are already strong. The best prior program (score 0.58) achieved slope_changes of only 41.2 and smoothness of 0.33 by using an innovation-adaptive constant-velocity Kalman filter before its smoothing stage. The insight: a Kalman pre-filter that collapses process noise when innovations are noise-sized removes most of the white noise before the polynomial fit, so the robust quadratic stage no longer reacts to noise-driven directional reversals — directly reducing slope_changes and false_reversals. Because the Kalman state models slope, its level estimate extrapolates trends, so the added stage contributes near-zero phase lag, protecting the already-good lag_error and responsiveness metrics. I insert a lightweight adaptive Kalman pass (MAD-based measurement-noise estimate, innovation-driven Q scaling) before the robust weighted quadratic regression, keeping the same output-length contract.
